identity.title: Probing Multiphase Gas in Local Massive Elliptical Galaxies via Multiwavelength Observations

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report new observations, including SOFIA \[CII\], ALMA CO, MUSE H$\alpha$+\[NII\] and VLA radio observations. These are complemented by a large suite of multiwavelength archival datasets

In this paper we present new far-infrared \[CII\] observations of a sample of 6 local massive elliptical galaxies taken with the Field-Imaging Far-Infrared Line Spectrometer (FIFI-LS) on board of SOFIA (cite: young12; temi14).

findings_qualitative.value: SOFIA FIFI-LS detects [CII] 157.74 um emission in 3 of the 6 observed massive elliptical galaxies (NGC 4203, NGC 4261, and NGC 4406) and sets upper limits in NGC 4374, NGC 4552, and NGC 4649.

evidence.quote: SOFIA FIFI-LS observations reveal \[CII\] line emission in 3 (NGC 4203, NGC 4261 and NGC 4406) out of 6 observed galaxies.

findings_qualitative.value: In the non-central galaxies of the sample, the detected cool gas is centrally concentrated and compact (often in rotating sub-kpc disks), in contrast to the extended filamentary structures seen in group-centered ellipticals.

evidence.quote: The distribution of the detected cool gas phase in our six (non-central) galaxies is often centrally concentrated and compact, at variance with the cold gas-rich galaxies studied in (cite: werner14).

findings_qualitative.value: Kinematical and morphological misalignments between the multiphase gas/dust and the stars, along with a two-order-of-magnitude spread in molecular gas mass at similar stellar luminosity, indicate that stellar mass loss is not the primary driver of the cold gas.

evidence.quote: Misalignment between the multiphase gas and stars suggest that stellar mass loss is not the primary driver.

Thus, these additional data confirm the lack of dependence of the molecular gas content on the stellar mass, with the implication that stellar mass loss is not the primary source of molecular gas in these galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: Cool gas in local massive non-central elliptical galaxies originates primarily from stellar mass loss.
claims.experiment: Compare spatial morphology and kinematics of dust, CO, Halpha+[NII], and [CII] with stellar axes, and examine molecular gas mass as a function of K-band stellar luminosity.
claims.result: Cold/warm gas and dust disks are often misaligned by up to ~90 degrees with respect to the stars (e.g., NGC 4261, NGC 4374), and molecular gas mass spans ~2 orders of magnitude while L_K varies by less than a factor of 2.
claims.finding: Stellar mass loss is not the primary source of molecular gas in these massive elliptical galaxies.

evidence.quote: Misalignment between the multiphase gas and stars suggest that stellar mass loss is not the primary driver.

The molecular gas content in our galaxy sample, as shown in Figure 14 and Table [\[tab:CII_CO_gal\]](#tab:CII_CO_gal), covers approximately 2 orders of magnitude, while the $L_K$ luminosity is within a factor of two.

claims.hypothesis: The multiphase gas properties and hot gas thermodynamics of the sample are regulated by top-down condensation and Chaotic Cold Accretion (CCA) in an AGN feeding/feedback cycle.
claims.experiment: Compare X-ray thermodynamic profiles, k-plot kinematics (velocity dispersion vs velocity shift), C-ratio = t_cool / t_eddy profiles, and VLA radio jet properties against CCA simulation predictions.
claims.result: Cool-gas-free galaxies (NGC 4649, NGC 4552) show high central pressure, smooth entropy maps, and weak radio jets; cool-gas-rich non-central galaxies fall within CCA k-plot contours and have C-ratio < 1 within r < 1 kpc, whereas central galaxy NGC 4636 has low C-ratio out to ~3 kpc.
claims.finding: Cool-gas-free galaxies are in the overheated quiescent phase of the AGN cycle, while galaxies with cool gas are in the CCA feeding phase, with non-central galaxies developing an inner sub-kpc condensation rain and central galaxies developing an extended rain.

evidence.quote: Comparing with Chaotic Cold Accretion (CCA) simulations, we find that our cool gas-free galaxies are likely in the overheated phase of the self-regulated AGN cycle, while for our galaxies with cool gas the k-plot and AGN power correlation corroborate the phase of CCA feeding
The related C-ratio further shows that central/non-central galaxies are expected to generate an extended/inner rain, consistent with our sample.

why_this_data.value: SOFIA FIFI-LS [CII] observations were obtained to expand the Herschel PACS sample to the remaining nearby X-ray bright massive early-type galaxies from Dunn et al. (2010), complemented by ALMA, IRAM, VLA, HST, MUSE, and Chandra to probe all gas phases and AGN feedback.

evidence.quote: The goal of the SOFIA FIFI-LS observations was to expand the sample of early type galaxies observed in the \[CII\] line with Herschal PACS by obtaining a complete coverage of the sample of 18 nearby ($d<100$ Mpc), massive, X-ray bright early-type galaxies

The recently acquired SOFIA data are complemented with a large suite of multiwavelength observations available in literature which include, radio (ALMA, IRAM, VLA), optical (HST, SOAR and VMOS), IR (Spitzer, Herschel), and X-ray (Chandra) data.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: GALFIT single and multi-component (Sersic, Nuker, Ferrer) models were tried for HST stellar emission subtraction, but rejected in favor of photutils or red-filter linear models which matched the true stellar emission better.

evidence.quote: We tried several types of profile (Sersic, Nuker, Ferrer, etc.) with GALFIT, but our models from the photutils or the "red" filter seem to be closer to the true stellar emission for these galaxies.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Single-Gaussian fit to the NGC 4261 SOFIA [CII] line was rejected in favor of a two-Gaussian fit because chi^2 decreased by almost a factor of 3 and BIC decreased by 13.9.

evidence.quote: For NGC 4261, given the width and the shape of the detected \[CII\] feature, we performed a fit with 2 Gaussians (Figure 5). The resulting $\chi^2$ decreases significantly (by almost a factor 3), and the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) is reduced by 13.9, which strongly indicates that the two line model is favored.

limitations_admitted.value: High angular resolution ALMA 12 m array observations can resolve out large-scale diffuse CO emission (as seen in NGC 5044 where ALMA recovered only 20% of the IRAM 30m flux).

evidence.quote: Given the high angular resolution of the 12m array data, some diffuse CO component might have been filtered out by the interferometer such as was the case for NGC 5044 observations, where the ALMA CO(2-1) flux was only 20% of the IRAM-30m flux (cite: david14).

limitations_admitted.value: SOFIA FIFI-LS observations have coarse spatial resolution and low SNR, leaving the cool gas spatially under-resolved and requiring bright-pixel fitting or point-source assumptions.

evidence.quote: We chose to fit the brightest pixel instead of integrating over the source extent because of the poor signal-to-noise of the data.
Moreover, our cool gas is often under-resolved (especially with SOFIA), meaning that we are only able to capture larger associations of clouds, rather than single elements

limitations_admitted.value: Systematic errors on HST Halpha+[NII] fluxes from imperfect continuum subtraction are likely underestimated due to residual point sources.

evidence.quote: Due to residual point sources affecting the H$\alpha+\rm [NII]$ images, it is likely that we have underestimated this error to some degree.

limitations_admitted.value: Small sample size prevents a robust statistical correlation analysis between AGN jet power P_jet and Halpha luminosity or cold gas mass.

evidence.quote: The limited data available does not allow for a robust analysis of correlations between the $P_{\rm jet}$ and H$\alpha$ luminosity or the amount of cold gas.

referee_caveats_inferred: Comparing SOFIA FIFI-LS [CII] fluxes (12 arcsec pixel scale) with high-resolution ALMA CO interferometric fluxes (0.12-0.3 arcsec beam, MRS 4-5.6 arcsec) introduces severe aperture and spatial-filtering mismatches in the [CII]/CO ratios.
ALMA imaging and calibration parameters for the newly analyzed CO datasets (NGC 4636, NGC 4261, NGC 4649) are largely omitted.

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA, HST, Chandra, and VLA datasets were retrieved from public archives alongside new SOFIA, ALMA, and MUSE observations.

evidence.quote: some of the data retrieved from public archives have not been published yet, and forms a set of original and new observations.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.01107.S, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.00301.S, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.00830.S.
